content.comment_body: I've posted several questions about building a meterage counter for an extrusion line and received very helpful responses. Good news—I managed to make it work! While my solution may not be the most efficient or elegant, it is functional. I'm willing to share the program ([article_no]) if anyone wants to review it. I welcome suggestions or critique. Also, is it possible to directly control each block on a [product_name] operator device? Thanks to everyone who contributed advice; I couldn't have succeeded without your support.

Congratulations on your achievement! Thank you for appreciating the input from forum members. It's beneficial for the community when users update on the outcomes of the advice given by members and experts, rather than leaving after finding a solution. Your feedback helps the continuous improvement of this space. Thanks again.

I've decided to upload the program to get input from other experts on possible improvements. A few notes: the four function keys set the preset meterage, I5 serves as the count input, and I7 is required for a reel change and reset. I1 initiates the winder, which must be active for the counter to operate. I5 is configured as a frequency input, with a maximum value of 4100 corresponding to 123 meters per minute. Enjoy!
